insight.title: Why do prices change all the time?
insight.subtitle: Understanding the balance between what we want and what is available.

sections.text: Imagine you are at a market. If everyone wants the same red apple, but there is only one left, the seller can charge more. This is called high demand. When many people want a limited item, its value goes up. This simple rule dictates the cost of almost everything you buy today.

The opposite is also true. If a shop has too many boxes of cookies and nobody wants them, the price will drop. The shop lowers the cost to encourage people to take them. This is called high supply. Businesses constantly watch these two forces to decide how much to charge for their goods.

This balance happens everywhere, from gas stations to toy stores. When materials are hard to find, prices rise. When new technology makes production easier, prices often fall. By looking at supply and demand, we can understand why our money buys more or less each day. It is the hidden heartbeat of our global economy.
